title: Bounded constructible complexes with field coefficients form a triangulated subcategory
statement:
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme and $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$. The full subcategory
$\Dbc(X,\Lambda)\subseteq D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ contains $0$, is closed under
isomorphisms and under the shifts $[\pm1]$, and if two vertices of a distinguished triangle
lie in $\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$ then so does the third. Hence it is a triangulated subcategory, and
it is thick.

proof.text: Work throughout with the actual coefficient sheaf $\Lambda_X$, pulled back from the condensed ring, and put $\mathcal A=\Mod(\Lambda_X)$. Use the universe and small-skeleton convention [def-weil-size-convention], so the site is small relative to the module universe. Then $\mathcal A$ is abelian by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and its cohomology functors are those of [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves], which applies to any sheaf of commutative rings, not just a constant sheaf. By [det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude] (2), membership in $\Dbc$ means finite cohomological support and constructibility of every cohomology sheaf. The zero sheaf has a finite constant local model, using the zero finitely presented module in [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model], so it is constructible on the one-stratum stratification (the empty stratification if $X$ is empty). The zero complex therefore belongs to $\Dbc$. An isomorphism of complexes in the derived category induces isomorphisms on all cohomology sheaves by functoriality; the same local models and stratification work for an isomorphic sheaf. Thus $\Dbc$ is closed under isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 03DA (lemma-abelian); blueprint proof, first paragraph: zero and isomorphisms

proof.text: For every integer $n$, [lem-sp-derived-cohomology-shift] applied to $\mathcal A$ gives $\mathcal H^q(K[n])\simeq\mathcal H^{q+n}(K)$. If the support of the cohomology of $K$ is contained in a finite set $S\subset\mathbf Z$, that of $K[n]$ is contained in $S-n$. Each of these cohomology sheaves is constructible by the isomorphism invariance established in step 1. The definition [det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude] (2) now gives $K[n]\in\Dbc$ for every $n$, in particular $n=1,-1$.

source.place: Tag 011H (definition-cohomology-shift); blueprint proof, first paragraph: shifts

proof.text: Let $K\xrightarrow uK'\xrightarrow vK''\to K[1]$ be distinguished with $K,K'\in\Dbc$. In the derived category of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], by [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] for the abelian category $\mathcal A$, there is an exact sequence $\mathcal H^qK\to\mathcal H^qK'\to\mathcal H^qK''\xrightarrow{\delta^q}\mathcal H^{q+1}K\to\mathcal H^{q+1}K'$ for each $q$. Choose finite cohomological supports $S$ for $K$ and $S'$ for $K'$. If $q\notin S'\cup(S-1)$, exactness gives $0\to\mathcal H^qK''\to0$, so $\mathcal H^qK''=0$. Thus the third vertex has finite cohomological support, as required by [det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude] (2).

source.place: Tag 05RS (lemma-cohomology-homological: on the homotopy category), Tag 0147 (definition-homological), and Tag 05RU (definition-unbounded-derived-category: the localization and descended cohomology); blueprint proof, second paragraph

proof.text:
Write the five consecutive terms of step 3 as $A\xrightarrow f B\xrightarrow g C\xrightarrow h D\xrightarrow k E$. Exactness says $\ker g=\operatorname{im}f$, $\ker h=\operatorname{im}g$ and $\operatorname{im}h=\ker k$. In the abelian category of [def-sp-abelian], every epimorphism is the cokernel of its kernel and every monomorphism is the kernel of its cokernel. The induced map $B/\ker g\to C$ is monic by [lem-weil-pbc-coimage-mono], with image $\ker h$; since $B/\ker g=B/\operatorname{im}f=\operatorname{coker}f$, and $C\to\operatorname{im}h=\ker k$ is epic with that kernel, this gives the short exact sequence
$$0\to\operatorname{coker}(\mathcal H^q u)\to\mathcal H^qK''\to\ker(\mathcal H^{q+1}u)\to0.$$
The endpoints are constructible by the kernel and cokernel clause of [det-lem-coefficient-heart-closure], since the four cohomology sheaves of $K,K'$ are constructible. Its extension clause then makes $\mathcal H^qK''$ constructible. The hypothesis is satisfied: $X$ is Noetherian and the coefficients are exactly $E$ or $\Qlb$; no assertion for arbitrary condensed coefficients or finite discrete coefficients is substituted. Combining this for all $q$ with step 3 proves $K''\in\Dbc$.

source.place: Tag 06UQ (lemma-cohomology-in-serre-subcategory), proof via the long exact sequence; abelian image/coimage identity is Tag 0109 (definition-abelian-category); blueprint proof, second paragraph

proof.text: The rotation axiom in [def-weil-triangulated-category] gives the other two cases explicitly. If $K',K''\in\Dbc$, rotate to $K'\to K''\to K[1]\to K'[1]$ and apply steps 3--4 to get $K[1]\in\Dbc$, hence $K\in\Dbc$ by step 2. If $K,K''\in\Dbc$, rotate twice to $K''\to K[1]\to K'[1]\to K''[1]$ and obtain $K'[1]\in\Dbc$, hence $K'\in\Dbc$. Consequently every distinguished triangle with two vertices in $\Dbc$ has its third there. Together with zero, isomorphism closure and all shifts, this is the full triangulated-subcategory criterion in [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory]; the ambient category is triangulated by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Thus $\Dbc$ has the inherited triangulated structure.

source.place: Tag 0145 (definition-triangulated), Tag 05QM (definition-triangulated-subcategory), Tag 05QX (lemma-triangulated-subcategory); blueprint proof, parenthetical rotation argument

proof.text: For thickness, let $L\in\Dbc$ and let $K$ be any retract of $L$ in the ambient derived category, with $i:K\to L$, $p:L\to K$ and $pi=1_K$. Fix $q$ and put $M=\mathcal H^qK$, $F=\mathcal H^qL$, $a=\mathcal H^q(i)$, $b=\mathcal H^q(p)$. Functoriality in [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] gives $ba=1_M$. Then $a$ identifies $M$ with $\ker(1_F-ab)$: $(1_F-ab)a=0$, and whenever $(1_F-ab)t=0$ one has $t=a(bt)$, uniquely since $ba=1_M$. Both source and target of $1_F-ab$ are the constructible sheaf $F$, so the kernel clause of [det-lem-coefficient-heart-closure] makes $M$ constructible. If $F=0$, the equality $ba=1_M$ forces $M=0$; thus the cohomological support of $K$ is contained in that of $L$. By [det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude] (2), $K\in\Dbc$. In particular, take the inclusion and projection of either summand when $L=K_1\oplus K_2$. Hence $\Dbc$ is closed under direct summands and is thick. The complementary idempotent $1_F-ab$, rather than $ab$ itself, has the chosen summand as its kernel.
